- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.35) and forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.14) and forecast is rising, cap upward momentum; downward bias may be warranted.  
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., >0.8), forecast should not overshoot by more than 2–3% beyond recent peak; apply mean reversion if overshoot exceeds 1.5σ.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.00–0.20) and history shows volatility, reduce forecast smoothness; allow for 1–2% asymmetric error tolerance.  
- If true outcome deviates >5% from forecast in first 5–7 days, adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., drop >3% in first 3 days), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid lagged overreaction.
